text: Ouarzazate is easily reached by sharedindividual taxi by bus in an average journey time of 4 hours from Marrakech. up a hill and opposite the Kasbah Taourirt and immediately next to the Ibis (which looks lovely with a huge pool and big screen outside). The reception staff were very welcoming and we were very pleased with our room which contained a fridge and a safe. All rooms also have air con and satellite tv. They are advertised as having a balcony these are shared with your neighbour and also have no chairs All the public areas are very nice with a lovely pool area which never really seemed to get busy (towels provided at reception). The bar area is huge and has very reasonably priced drinks and snacks. Breakfast is served downstairs in the main restaurant and is very nice with a huge selection of food hot drinks and juices. We also ate dinner in the restaurant on our first night and had a very enjoyable meal. Many local people try and entice you in via any number of entrances. Note that there is an official entrance which is opposite the artisanal shopping complex which takes you into the Kasbah that has recently been restored (10dh). Ouarzazate town (which is much more modern than I was expecting) has quite a few shops a decent supermarket (bizarrely enough selling more alcohol and pork than anything else!) and a number of restaurants. I read somewhere that Chez Dimitri has changed its name to Café Mogador it hasnt! The 2 restaurants are miles apart! 2 fillet steaks 2 desserts water and coffee all for about 40 and it was the best steak wed eaten in a long time!!!! It was so good we ate there 2 nights is a row! The reception staff are very helpful and provided us with maps and organised an onward taxi to take us to Zagora. All in all the hotel made a lovely change to all the riads that wed been staying in and I would definitely recommend it - worthy of its 4 stars definitely!
label: positive
